c1ec407a6df510b1ef272075ca397e45cb387a16.summary: The page is titled as a report on CaddyWiper, a wiper malware said to target Ukrainian organizations, and carries an IBM byline. The body contains no threat content: only a long list of IBM-owned web properties, a source line and a page count. No actors, dates, tools, techniques, CVEs or figures appear in the text, so nothing can be recorded as a fact.

c133b079fdfe661f8e64e8d0ccf512f5668e1592.summary: Malpedia family page for the DarkSide ransomware. Its only description is a single sentence attributing a view of DarkSide as a C-written ransomware to FireEye. The rest of the page is an index of roughly 200 dated article titles, with vendor or media names and authors, about DarkSide and related ransomware groups. The page itself does not analyse a campaign, actor, or incident, so it is not treated as a threat report.

c113d860308817fd565d73657bc12da6d142c7bd.summary: FortiGuard Labs blog post by Axelle Apvrille reverse-engineers ELF/Sshdinjector.A!tr, a Linux malware collection injected into the SSH daemon. Samples surfaced around mid-November 2024. A dropper installs a malicious library, libsshd.so, which connects to a bot master and typically exfiltrates information. Other binaries keep the host infected. The post says the collection is attributed to the DaggerFly espionage group in existing threat intelligence. It also evaluates generative AI (r2ai with Claude 3.5 Sonnet) as a reverse-engineering aid, reporting hallucination, extrapolation and…

c1f9f0d2d77c1b350c7195058c7ac7bed463957a.summary: Intezer report (28 July 2020) on the Ngrok Mining Botnet, which abuses publicly exposed Docker API servers in cloud environments. Attackers use a container escape to reach the host, then schedule scanner and downloader scripts via cron. The report also describes Doki, a previously undetected Linux backdoor that finds its C2 through a Dogecoin-blockchain-based domain generation method. Doki was first uploaded to VirusTotal on January 14, 2020.
